rows.selection_reason: 1) Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been completed, so there is no performance reference and no information about which design axes (modality, profile setting, encoder choice, aggregation, fusion) actually matter. The highest-priority uncertainty is establishing a baseline performance level for a multimodal model using standard, well-motivated components. 2) What this tests: config_051 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, resnet50, concat) is a clean multimodal baseline that uses a learned single-cell RNA encoder (scgpt), a standard image backbone (resnet50), a single profile (eliminating the aggregation variable entirely), and the simplest fusion (concat). It establishes the reference performance for the study's core question—whether combining RNA and image modalities is informative—while keeping every other design choice at its most standard value. 3) Why it is the best first experiment: Starting with the simplest reasonable multimodal configuration on the study's main path (rather than a fully complex multiprofile/transformer/weighted setup) means that in subsequent experiments we can add one axis of complexity at a time (e.g., multiprofile + aggregation, a different RNA encoder, a stronger image backbone, weighted fusion) and attribute performance changes to that single change. It also avoids the risk that a poor result is confounded by multiple simultaneously exotic choices. This maximizes the information gained per experiment under the limited budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_051: multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, resnet50, concat → acc 0.427), the most critical uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion actually provides a meaningful advantage over a unimodal baseline. config_018 (rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt) is the cleanest single-factor comparison: it is identical to config_051 except the image modality is removed. If RNA-only performs comparably (~0.42–0.44), the image contributes little and we should focus budget on RNA representation and profile/aggregation choices. If RNA-only is substantially lower, the image is a key signal and we should next explore image encoder variants (e.g., imagenet_vit_l). This experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most fundamental design decision (multimodal vs. unimodal) before committing further experiments to more complex multimodal configurations.

Evidence: config_051 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt+resnet50, concat) achieved 0.4275 acc vs config_018 (rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt) at 0.4106, suggesting a modest multimodal benefit. However, with only two data points, we have no information on whether multiprofile adds value over singleprofile—a decision that affects roughly half the search space. Question: Does multiprofile (with the simplest aggregation, avgpool) improve over singleprofile when all other factors (scgpt RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, concat fusion) are held constant? Why this is the best next experiment: config_002 is the most controlled comparison to config_051, changing only profile_setting (single→multi) and adding the minimally necessary aggregation (avgpool). If multiprofile+avgpool does not clearly beat 0.4275, it strongly suggests multiprofile is not the key lever and we can focus budget on singleprofile variants (fusion, encoders). If it does improve, it validates the multiprofile direction and motivates testing transformer aggregation next. This single experiment reduces the largest remaining architectural uncertainty with minimal confounding variables.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, acc=0.512) substantially outperforms singleprofile with no aggregation (config_051, acc=0.427), an ~8.5-point gap. This tells us that combining multiple profiles helps, but it does not tell us whether the aggregation *mechanism* matters or whether the gain is simply from having more data to average. Config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, transformer, concat) is a single-variable change from config_002, swapping only avgpool for transformer aggregation. If transformer significantly improves over avgpool, it indicates profiles carry heterogeneous information requiring structured combination, justifying further investment in aggregation design. If the gain is marginal, it confirms simple averaging is sufficient and we should redirect budget toward other axes (e.g., image encoder or fusion method). This is the most informative next step because it isolates the aggregation decision while holding all other design choices at their currently best-known values.

Evidence: config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the best at 0.5121, far exceeding config_051 (multimodal, singleprofile) at 0.4275, confirming multiprofile is a major driver. However, the multimodal-vs-rna_only gap at singleprofile is only ~1.7% (config_051 vs config_018), which is weak and possibly noise. We have no multiprofile rna_only baseline to determine whether the image modality is actually contributing at the multiprofile level. Question: config_008 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) is a clean single-variable ablation of config_002—removing only the image modality. If it performs near 0.51, the image adds little and we can simplify; if it drops substantially, the image is essential and we should invest in image-encoder choices (e.g., ViT-L). Why this is best: under a limited budget, resolving whether the image modality is a meaningful contributor is the highest-value uncertainty to reduce before committing further experiments to image-encoder or fusion variations. It also guards against over-investing in a more complex multimodal pipeline if a simpler rna_only multiprofile model is competitive.

Evidence: Multi-profile with avgpool aggregation is clearly the strongest setting (config_008 rna_only=0.5305, config_002 multimodal=0.5121), and avgpool outperforms transformer aggregation (0.5121 vs 0.4710). Notably, the RNA-only model (config_008) slightly outperforms the multimodal counterpart (config_002) by ~1.8%, suggesting the image modality with concat fusion may not be contributing effectively. Question: Is the suboptimal fusion strategy (concat) the reason the image modality underperforms? Config_048 isolates a single variable—changing fusion from concat to weighted—while holding model_setting, profile_setting, rna_encoder, image_encoder, and aggregation identical to config_002. This gives a clean A/B comparison on fusion and a three-way benchmark against config_008 (RNA-only). Why best next step: It is the most targeted experiment to determine whether the image channel can be made useful with scgpt+resnet50, which directly informs whether to invest remaining budget in image-encoder or fusion variations versus committing to RNA-only or alternative RNA encoders. A single-variable change maximizes information per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: The best multimodal config (config_048: multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.525, while the best rna_only config (config_008: multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) achieves 0.530. This suggests the image modality with ResNet50 has not yet provided a clear advantage over RNA alone. The most important open question is whether a stronger image encoder (ImageNet ViT-L) can make the multimodal model outperform the RNA-only baseline. config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) differs from config_048 only in the image encoder, making it a clean single-variable comparison. If it outperforms both config_048 and config_008, it confirms that image information is valuable but was underexploited by ResNet50; if it does not, it strongly supports that the image modality is not contributing meaningfully in this task, redirecting effort toward RNA encoder or aggregation choices. This is the highest-information experiment under the limited budget because it resolves the central question of whether multimodality is worth pursuing.

All seven completed experiments use scgpt as the RNA encoder, leaving the RNA representation choice as the largest unexplored design dimension. The current best config (config_019: scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile, acc=0.542) establishes a strong baseline. config_007 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) is an exact A/B comparison that changes only the RNA encoder from scgpt to pca_n2000, isolating the effect of learned vs. linear RNA representations. If PCA performs comparably, it indicates the task does not require a complex RNA encoder and simplifies the design space; if it underperforms significantly, it confirms that a learned representation is essential and motivates further comparison with scvi_n200. This single-variable experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about one of the most impactful design choices while keeping all other settings at their empirically best values (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted, imagenet_vit_l), making it the highest-information next step under a limited budget.

1) Evidence: config_007 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted + multiprofile) achieved 0.635 acc, a dramatic ~9-point jump over config_019 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l, same other settings) at 0.542. This strongly implicates the RNA encoder as the dominant factor. However, we also know imagenet_vit_l modestly outperforms resnet50 with scgpt (config_019: 0.542 vs config_048: 0.525). 2) Question: config_006 (pca_n2000 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted + multiprofile) is a single-variable swap of the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50, directly comparing against config_007. This isolates whether the 0.635 result is driven primarily by the RNA representation (pca_n2000) or requires the specific combination with imagenet_vit_l. 3) Why best next experiment: This is the cleanest, most informative single-variable test from the current best configuration. If pca_n2000 + resnet50 performs comparably, it confirms the RNA encoder is the key lever and the image encoder is secondary—guiding all future experiments toward RNA representation choices. If it drops substantially, it reveals a critical interaction effect. Either outcome sharply reduces uncertainty about which design axis to prioritize under a limited budget, making this the highest-information-value experiment available.

The strongest evidence so far is that pca_n2000 as RNA encoder dramatically outperforms scgpt (~0.64 vs ~0.51-0.54 accuracy). However, with scgpt, rna_only multiprofile avgpool (config_008: 0.530) actually outperformed the corresponding multimodal setup (config_002: 0.512), suggesting the image modality may not be adding value with that encoder. The critical open question is whether this pattern holds for pca_n2000: does the image encoder contribute meaningfully on top of an already strong RNA representation? config_022 (rna_only, pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool) is a clean single-factor comparison against config_006 (multimodal, pca_n2000, resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted: 0.639), isolating the effect of the image modality. If rna_only pca_n2000 approaches or exceeds 0.639, it reveals the image is redundant and redirects the search toward simpler RNA-only pipelines; if it falls well below, it confirms the multimodal benefit and justifies further multimodal exploration. Under a limited budget, resolving this fundamental design question is more informative than fine-tuning aggregation or fusion within the already-promising multimodal pca_n2000 space.
